instructions: Monitors a school-run drive and pings leave-by times for morning drop-off and afternoon pickup, adjusting for live traffic and construction.

view.description: Monitors a school-run drive and pings leave-by times for morning drop-off and afternoon pickup, adjusting for live traffic and construction.

memory.content: School-run leave-by workflow: the user drives from home to school for drop-off and pickup. Drop-off and pickup have target arrival times; baseline leave times apply when traffic is normal. Unpredictable construction or congestion on the route should be treated as authoritative over baselines.

Weekday leave-by pings for the school run fire in morning and afternoon windows before the drop-off and pickup targets, using live traffic. On later checks the same window, stay quiet unless the leave-by moved earlier by 3+ minutes or a new snag appeared.
Live drive times are looked up in Google Maps (browser) with traffic enabled; no dedicated maps connector is required.

skills.content:
---
name: school-run-setup
description: >-
  Use this when setting up or changing the school-run route, arrival targets,
  baseline leave times, or check windows for leave-by pings.
---
Collect and save the facts needed for school-run leave-by monitoring, then create or update the morning and afternoon leave-by routines.

Ask for, one topic at a time if needed:
- Home address (drive origin)
- School name and address (drive destination)
- Drop-off target arrival time and school start time
- Pickup target arrival time
- Baseline leave times when traffic is normal
- Timezone if not already known
- Whether checks should run weekdays only (default) or include weekends

Save durable route and timing facts to agent memory (profile tier for the standing route; log for schedule changes).

Create or update two weekday routines (local timezone):
1. Morning drop-off leave-by — several checks in the window before the usual leave time (e.g. about 25, 15, and 5 minutes before baseline leave).
2. Afternoon pickup leave-by — several checks in the window before the usual leave time.

Each routine should: look up live drive time with traffic (Google Maps or similar), compute leave-by for the target arrival plus a small kids/doors buffer (about 2–3 minutes), notify in chat with leave time + drive duration + one line if worse than baseline, and on later runs the same window only re-notify if leave-by moved earlier by 3+ minutes or a new snag appeared.

Do not hard-code another family's addresses or times; always use this user's values.

routines.name: Morning school drop-off leave-by
routines.description: Weekday mornings before drop-off: check live drive time and ping a leave-by time.
routines.content:
Weekday morning school drop-off traffic check.

Route: FROM [HOME ADDRESS] TO [SCHOOL NAME AND ADDRESS]. Target arrival: [DROP-OFF ARRIVAL TIME] (school starts [SCHOOL START TIME]). Baseline leave without bad traffic is about [MORNING BASELINE LEAVE]. Construction or unpredictable traffic on the route — treat live traffic as authoritative.

Look up the current driving time WITH traffic for that route (use a maps/directions source that shows live traffic, such as Google Maps in the browser). Compute when they should leave to arrive by the drop-off target, including a small buffer for kids/doors (about 2–3 minutes). Note any construction delays, incidents, or unusually slow segments called out on the map.

Notify them in chat with a short leave-by: the recommended leave time, current ETA / drive duration, and one line on why if traffic is worse than the usual baseline drive. On later runs the same morning, only notify again if the leave-by time moved earlier by 3+ minutes or a new snag appeared; otherwise stay quiet.

If the lookup fails, say so briefly and fall back to leaving a few minutes earlier than the baseline leave time unless they already know of a problem.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 15,25,35 7 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Afternoon school pickup leave-by
routines.description: Weekday afternoons before pickup: check live drive time and ping a leave-by time.
routines.content:
Weekday afternoon school pickup traffic check.

Route: FROM [HOME ADDRESS] TO [SCHOOL NAME AND ADDRESS] (pickup). Target arrival: [PICKUP ARRIVAL TIME]. Baseline leave without bad traffic is about [AFTERNOON BASELINE LEAVE]. Construction or unpredictable traffic on the route — treat live traffic as authoritative.

Look up the current driving time WITH traffic for that route (use a maps/directions source that shows live traffic, such as Google Maps in the browser). Compute when they should leave to arrive by the pickup target, with a couple minutes of buffer. Note any construction delays, incidents, or unusually slow segments.

Notify them in chat with a short leave-by: the recommended leave time, current ETA / drive duration, and one line on why if traffic is worse than the usual baseline drive. On later runs the same afternoon, only notify again if the leave-by time moved earlier by 3+ minutes or a new snag appeared; otherwise stay quiet.

If the lookup fails, say so briefly and fall back to leaving a few minutes earlier than the baseline leave time unless they already know of a problem.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 20,35,45 14 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
